elements.problem: Unresponsive is a reasonable match for 'does not respond to voice or physical stimulation'.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient unresponsive, pulseless or not breathing :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unresponsive" "finding"))
Check for emergency patient airway, breathing and circulation signs :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unresponsive" "finding"))

elements.problem: 'Or unsure' is not representable; absent pulse captured.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient unresponsive, pulseless or not breathing :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Absent pulse" "finding"))

elements.problem: 'Not breathing' = Apnea, 'gasping' covered. Note the page branch applies only when pulse is felt; Emergency regardless is fine.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient unresponsive, pulseless or not breathing :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Gasping for breath" "finding")) / "Agonal respiration" / "Apnea"

elements.problem: Airway obstruction signs encoded. Neck-injury jaw-thrust branch is management only.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Respiratory obstruction" "disorder")) / "Snoring" / "Gurgling" / "Noisy respiration"

elements.problem: Threshold and direction right. Concept 'Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen' (SaO2) is arguably not the pulse-oximetry SpO2 concept; worth a SNOMED check.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Difficulty breathing" "finding")) ; (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen" ...) %) 94)

elements.problem: GCS assessment captured via total-score findings.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Glasgow coma scale, 3" "finding")) ... "Glasgow coma scale, 8"

elements.problem: BP < 90/60 split into SBP<90 or DBP<60 (reasonable). Footnote 3 acute heart failure signs encoded. Atropine itself is management.
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (and (< (measurement "Pulse, function" bpm) 50) (or (< SBP 90) (< DBP 60) Decreased level of consciousness, Chest pain, Acute heart failure, (and Swelling of lower limb (or Orthopnea Dyspnea on exertion))))
Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (< (measurement "Respiratory rate" bpm) 9) ; Blue lips ; Blue tongue

parts_missing: Whether SBP<80 / pulse>=100 are meant as alternatives or together
elements.problem: Each of SBP<80, pulse>=100 alone triggers Emergency, whereas the footnote defines shock as a cluster; pulse>=100 alone as Emergency is probably over-triggering. Heavy bleeding encoded as Bleeding+Severe. 'Known heart problem / severe infection' only alters fluid choice (management).
evidence: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise :: (active_condition Shock) (< SBP 80) (>= Pulse 100) Bleeding+Severe

elements.problem: Page lists sudden breathlessness, more resonant/decreased breath sounds/pain on one side, deviated trachea as the features that make tension pneumothorax 'likely' (no 'and' stated). Rule requires sudden dyspnea AND deviated trachea AND one side sign, which is much stricter and would miss most true presentations. Also 'Trachea displaced' typed as disorder; it is a finding.
evidence: Diagnose probable tension pneumothorax (emergency patient) :: (and Dyspnea+Sudden onset (or Hyperresonance+Unilateral, Decreased breath sounds+Unilateral, Chest pain+Unilateral) Trachea displaced)

elements.problem: Footnote 3 lists SBP<80, pulse>=100, RR>30, confusion/restlessness, weakness as signs for 'shock likely'; the rule requires ALL of them (including weakness) simultaneously, so it will almost never fire. A 'consider' list is probably meant as any-of or a k-of-n. Also footnote 3 (leg swelling, difficulty breathing worse lying/with effort = acute heart failure) is encoded in the pulse<50 priority branch only; footnote 1 (life-limiting illness/CPR) is not logic.
evidence: Diagnose probable shock (emergency patient) :: (and (< SBP 80) (>= Pulse 100) (> RR 30) (or Clouded consciousness Acute confusion Restlessness) Asthenia)

rule_level_problems.problem: All criteria ANDed incl. asthenia; page footnote reads as a list of signs. Also the priority rule triggers on active_condition Shock, so a too-strict diagnosis silently weakens the pathway.
Requires sudden dyspnea AND deviated trachea AND one side sign; page lists them as features. Too strict; Emergency via this branch will rarely fire.

rule_level_problems.rule: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise
rule_level_problems.problem: SBP<80 and pulse>=100 each alone trigger Emergency; the page pairs them in the shock footnote. Also pulse<50 branch includes chest pain and acute heart failure as 'unstable' which is right, but single check_for item 'Chest pain' (no qualifier) used for both this and unilateral chest pain.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for emergency patient airway, breathing and circulation signs
rule_level_problems.problem: check_for contains Dyspnea on exertion, Asthenia, Swelling of lower limb etc. but not the diastolic BP measurement; trigger 'or' also lacks diastolic BP/unstable-pulse composite, so the task may not fire for isolated hypertension-free low-DBP bradycardia (pulse<50 already triggers, so minor).
No possible/probable diagnosis for other items; page only has tension pneumothorax and shock 'likely', both present. No flowchart-level problems apart from 'unsure' pulse not representable.

summary: The two 'likely' diagnosis rules (tension pneumothorax and shock) are over-strict conjunctions of what the page lists as features, so they will rarely fire and Emergency via those routes is weakened. Everything else on the red box (unresponsive/pulseless/gasping, airway noises, SpO2<94, RR<9, cyanosis, bradycardia-unstable, GCS<=8, heavy bleeding) is encoded with right thresholds; pulse>=100 and SBP<80 each alone as Emergency is arguably over-triggering.
